title: Define SLA acceptance matrix and tenant-priority burst-recovery playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD to establish an acceptance matrix for SLA/SLO assertions across mixed workloads (chat, embeddings, reranking) plus a tenant-weighted burst recovery and error-budget-transfer playbook. This ticket captures scope, acceptance criteria, rollout gate definitions, and required telemetry/alerts. Goal: make rollout decisions deterministic when regional or cross-tenant bursts occur and provide clear, testable canary exit/rollback rules. This PRD complements existing per-tenant SLO docs but focuses specifically on coordinated error budget transfers, short-term burst shielding, and deterministic canary exit behavior.
scope_clarifications: Include hosted API and Dedicated; exclude on-prem Private initially (follow-up ticket will cover air-gapped constraints)
Define SLOs for 3 workload classes: interactive-chat, async-embeddings, and batch-rerank
Cover both p50/p95/p99 latency bands and availability (successful responses) plus an operational 'degraded mode' definition
Specify telemetry required for canary probes and burn-rate calculations
Provide step-by-step rollback and canary-exit checklist usable by on-call and SRE
acceptance_criteria: A matrix document (PDF/Confluence) exists mapping workload class x tenant-priority to target p50/p95/p99 latency envelopes and availability thresholds
For each cell in the matrix, a numeric error budget (per 30d window) and a fast-burn threshold are defined
Canary policy defined: minimum probe traffic, probe success criteria, probe burn-rate calculation, and explicit exit/rollback thresholds for two consecutive probe windows
A documented error-budget-transfer policy exists that allows temporary reallocation of error budget from low-priority tenants to protect high-priority tenants during regional bursts
Playbook steps (operator checklist) for entering/exiting degraded mode with command examples and dashboard links are included
Automated contract tests (CI) are defined to validate SLO assertions against synthetic probe traces and will run on PRs that change routing or batching logic
User-visible degradation messaging contract is specified (what status codes and client-side hints to return when degraded)
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Trade-off: aggressive tenant shielding reduces impact to high-priority tenants but increases latency/failed requests for low-priority tenants. Decision: adopt temporary error-budget transfer with a time-boxed window (max 2 hours) and automated decay back to baseline
Trade-off: canary probe frequency vs false positives. Decision: use dual-window (1 minute & 10 minute aggregates) to balance sensitivity and stability
Trade-off: complexity of per-tenant live adjustments vs operational risk. Decision: implement transfer as a staged workflow requiring SRE approval for transfers > 30% of a tenant's error budget
Decision: initial rollout excludes Private on-prem deployments to avoid adding networked authorization complexity; follow-up PRD will handle that scope
notes: This ticket synthesizes inputs from Runtime (batching & KV cache) and Console (observability) teams
We must align metric names with the runtime telemetry schema to ensure contract tests can read p99 latency and error counts
Estimate assumes 2 sprint collaboration between PM, Eng, and SRE to complete docs + CI tests
Linked dashboards will be created under /dashboards/operational-contracts/SLA-matrix once PRD approved
